title: Disconnect callback function is called before server->num_connected_clients is decremented
body:
I'd like to store the state of my game server once all players have left. However, netcode calls `connect_disconnect_callback_function()` before `server->num_connected_clients--;`, which means that the number of connect clients is 1 when the last disconnect callback fires.

I thought about moving the callback to the bottom, but it seems like a good amount of metadata about the connection is reset that may be useful to those subscribing to the callback (yojimbo for example).

Would it make sense to move the `    server->num_connected_clients--;` line to before `connect_disconnect_callback_function()` in `netcode_server_disconnect_client_internal`?

Max

nodes.body:
I have thought about this some more. The reason the number of connected clients is not decremented, is that the idea is that this callback gets called *before* we disconnect that client. This is intentional. This way, you can trust that all data for the client that is disconnecting is intact at in the callback.

So, to work around this, you can do your cleanup when num_connected_clients == 1, or if you wish yourself, Do the decrement yourself on a copy of the num connected clients queried from the netcode server, and run your logic on that, if you want it to look clean.

Keeping it this way is the best for consistency. Note that the inverse happens for join, the client joins, and then the callback happens *after* everything is setup for that client, so the first join also has num_connected_clients == 1 when the callback fires. Again, intentional.

I know this may seem a bit strange, but it's the safest way to offer all the client data to the callback, without firing a callback on client disconnect after you've nuked the connected client...

Are you ok with me renaming these methods to `OnServerDidConnectClient(int clientIndex)` / `OnServerWillDisconnectClient(int clientIndex)`? That's how I name methods when I follow this same pattern in my own libraries.
No thanks! Please leave them as they are. We don't want to break the interface for other users of the library.
